Tha Àtaidh agus Tilidh a’ dol a chèilidh air Blor is tha e a’ sèideadh builgean mòr an urra dhaibh, airson is gun tèid acasan ri sgèith san adhar cuideachd. Tha iad a’ dol nas àirde is nas àirde is nas àirde, is tha an t-eagal air Àtaidh. It is extremely windy and Neep has a wonderful time flying through the air on a whirligig. Abney and Teal go to see Bop - who blows a giant bubble for each of them so they can join in. They go higher and higher, which Abney is not too sure about…

programme.title: Sionnach agus Maigheach (Fox & Hare)
programme.desc: Tha Sionnach a’ lorg dìsinn am measg stuth a chaidh a chaith gu aon taobh. Tha an dìsinn a’ còrdadh ri Comhachag agus tha e a’ dèanamh iomlaid air a shon leis an dèideag as fheàrr leis. Tha Sionnach air a dhòigh leis an dèideag ùr ach tha Comhachag ga h-ionndrainn gu mòr. Owl really likes it too and decides to trade it for his favourite doll, Oehoe. Fox enjoys life with his new toy, but Owl comes to realise he made a huge mistake; he misses Oehoe so much! Fox, however, won’t give it back. Hare thinks of a cunning way to solve the stand-off.

Tha Ms Sharpe agus cuid de na sgoilearan aice trang ag ullachadh airson a’ Mhòid, agus chan eil cùisean idir rèidh eadar Danny agus Mrs Fullerton. As the first term comes to an end, it’s evident that tensions are building at Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche. Miss Sharpe and her pupils are busy preparing for the Mòd and it’s looking as if Danny and Mrs Fullerton are out for revenge.

programme.title: Calum: Cogadh nan Comhlan
programme.desc: Tha Calum airson a chòmhlann aige a thoirt à Glaschu dhan Òban airson blàr mòr ciùil a tha dol aig a' Mhòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail. Ach, le tòrr fharpaisean agus gainead tìde, chan eil cùisean a' dol mar bu chòir. Leis nach eil e furasda còmhlan a làimhseachadh aig na h-amannan as fheàrr, saoil ciamar a thèid dhaibh leis na dùbhlain mhòra a th' air thoiseach orra... Calum aims to take his band from Glasgow to Oban for a major musical battle at the Royal National Mòd. However, with numerous competitions and time constraints, things aren't going according to plan. Managing a band is never easy even in the best of times - how will they cope with the significant challenges that lie ahead?

programme.title: A’ Chùil
programme.desc: Tha Choirstaidh air ais le prògram eile bhon stiùidio aice, A’ Chùil. Sa phrògram seo tha i a’ sireadh an “slime” as fheàrr, ach saoil dè an reasabaidh a bhios soirbheachail? An e “slime” cruasbach, “slime” a ghabhas ithe, “slime” bith-chnàmhach no “slime” molach? Choirstaidh is looking for the best slime recipe, but what will it be? Crunchy, edible, biodegradable or fluffy slime?

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc: Màiri Anna NicUalraig agus Liusaidh Cooke – An Còcaire Fiadhain – a’ rùrachd airson tairbheartas nàdair. Tha Liusaidh a’ toirt Màiri Anna dhachaigh gu dùthaich a h-òige, Shropshire, far an do thòisich a beatha an co-bhuinn ri nàdar. Tha iad a’ trusadh bhalgan-buachair nach gabh a lorg an Gàidhealtachd na h-Alba, agus a’ dèanamh picil leotha. Tha iad a’ beachdachadh air àrainneachd gu math eadar-dhealaichte bho an dachaigh an Alba le taic bho athair Liusaidh, a’ tadhal air darach a tha co-dhiù 800 bliadhn’ a dh’aois, agus a’ trusadh eidheann-thalmhainn, lus cùbhraidh a tha càirdeach do phionnd is sèids. Agus tha an còmhnaidh ùine ann airson basgaid ùir. Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke - The Wild Cooke -forage for nature’s bounty. Lucy takes Mary Ann to Shropshire where she grew up and began her life in harmony with nature. They collect fungi that can’t be found in Highland Scotland and pickle them. With some help from Lucy’s dad, they visit an 800-year-old oak tree and forage for ground ivy, a fragrant herb related to mint and sage. And there’s always time for a new basket. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Faodail
programme.desc: Tha Tasglann Fhilm Faodail a’ tarraing aire gu filmichean dhùthchasach Innse Gall bho na 1930an gu na 80an, a bha caillte ach a-nis glèidhte don ghinealach ri teachd. Tha bhana Cinema Sgìre Leantainneach a’ siubhal nan eilean, a’ taisbeanadh fhilmichean sna sgìrean ionadail, le cothrom am faicinn air-loidhne air feadh an t-saoghail. Cuirear aithris bheairteach ùr riutha, a’ buntainn ris a’ Ghàidhealtachd, airson luchd-amhairc an là an-diugh. The Faodail Film Archive celebrates lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s to the 1980s in the Outer Hebrides, preserving the archive for future generations. The Cinema Sgìre Continuing mobile cinema van travels the islands, showcasing footage to local communities, making them accessible globally online, and adding rich new narratives relevant to the Gàidhealtachd for contemporary audiences. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Samhradh air Sàl
programme.desc: Angus Mackay is joined by his daughter Ruth as they go to sea on a spectacular summer's day. Along the way they encounter a large pod of dolphins who take great delight in racing their small boat. Then it’s time for fishing and chat about the formative role of fishing in Ruth’s upbringing. Anns an dàrna prògram mu dheireadh san t-sreath, tha nighean Aonghais, Rut, còmhla ris agus iad aig muir air latha samhraidh eireachdail. Air an t-slighe, coinnichidh iad ri buidheann leumadairean-mara a tha dannsa mun eathar. Às dèidh sin, tha an t-àm ann airson iasgach agus còmhradh mun bhuaidh a bh’ aig iasgach air beatha Ruth.

Le agallamhan leis a’ chòmhlan is caraidean agus le criomagan bhon chonsairt. A special programme to celebrate 20 years of Skerryvore. The legendary Scottish band performed an anniversary show to thousands of fans in the spectacular surroundings of Floors Castle in the Scottish Borders. Featuring interviews with band members and friends, plus concert highlights. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Julie Fleeting
programme.desc: Determined to play, nine-year-old Julie Fleeting’s life in football began with a local boys club. It was the first step in achieving a dream she didn’t even know existed. From playing professionally in America to winning multiple honours with Arsenal, and scoring more goals for Scotland than anyone else, Julie has consistently inspired, empowered and led from the front. In a story of tenacity and triumph, Julie’s journey in football is also one of family, humility and respect. Thòisich Julie Fleeting a’ cluiche ball-coise còmhla ri sgioba bhalaich aig naoi bliadhna a dh’aois, a’ chiad cheum air an t-slighe gu dreuchd nach robh i fiù’s a smaointinn a bha comasach dhith. Bho bhith a’ cluiche gu proifeiseanta ann an Ameireagaidh gu togail dhuaisean aig Arsenal sa cur barrachd thadhail do dh’ Alba seach duine sam bith eile, tha Julie air a bhith na misneachd sna h-eisimpleir fad a beatha. Ach tha a slighe ann am ball-coise cuideachd mu dheidhinn theaghlach, irisleachd agus spèis. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.desc: Tha Caitlin na boireannach òg a th’air a beò-ghlacadh le bhith a’ coimhead air eòin. Nuair a smaoineachas sinn air a’ chur-seachad seo is mathaid nach e òigridh a’ chiad fheadhainn a thig a-steach oirnn - ach tha Caitlin airson seo atharrachadh. Anns a’ phrògram seo cluinnear na sgeulachdan pearsanta acasan mu na buannachdan agus mun mhòr-thlachd a tha iad a’ faighinn às a’ chur-seachad iongantach seo. Caitlin is an avid birdwatcher, but as a young female, she goes against stereotype. Keen to connect with people who share her passion, she sets off on a road trip around Scotland to meet other birders who are defying the typecasts and to uncover some of the personal stories behind the hobby. Together, they share the joys and frustrations of birdwatching as well as the pure exhilaration in spotting a bird that means so much to them. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.desc: Wildlife documentary featuring the fascinating lives of Britain's beautiful butterflies, filmed in exquisite detail and celebrating their enduring appeal to the British people. It opens up the intriguing possibility that a passion for butterflies could help us preserve the landscapes that we love.

Determined to restore his family’s reputation, Shakespeare works harder than ever, producing hit after hit: A Midsummer Night’s Dream, Henry IV and Julius Caesar. But as his star rises, a series of tragedies strike. Shakespeare’s life, purpose and family are thrown into chaos, and he begins to question if his new life is worth the sacrifice.

Joining The Amy Winehouse Band are special guests including Baby Rose, Corinne Bailey Rae, FLO, Jessie Reyez, Jorja Smith, Lianne La Havas, Nia Smith, Sasha Keable, Skye Newman, Terri Walker and Yebba, who all share their renditions of the tracks from the album. Her seminal and big-selling Back to Black album had been released the autumn before and by the time of this festival had become a huge success. She and her band perform many of her classic tracks, including Tears Dry on Their Own, Back to Black and, of course, Rehab.

programme.title: In Ten Pictures
programme.desc: Amy Winehouse’s image is known around the world. She was the north London girl with a unique voice and look, who became hugely successful seemingly overnight, and whose private life the press became obsessed by. She died in 2011, aged just 27. This documentary throws a unique lens onto an extraordinary life, focusing on ten defining photographs - from iconic shots to private snaps – with the stories behind them revealed by those who were there and those who knew her best, including her parents and close friends.

programme.title: Countryfile

Charlotte Smith and Joe Crowley head to Yr Wyddfa, Wales’s highest peak, to meet the people caring for its landscape and keeping visitors on the move. Joe joins volunteers tackling litter in some of the mountain’s hardest-to-reach gullies before discovering work to protect rare alpine plants and the elusive Snowdon beetle, found nowhere else in the UK. Meanwhile, Charlotte goes behind the scenes at Wales’s highest cafe to find out what it takes to keep visitors fed and watered at the summit. And Tom Heap investigates how organised crime gangs are targeting the countryside.

Rosie visits the dairy farm near Peterhead that diversified and created new markets for their milk, and Dougie steps out with a herd of rare Irish cattle.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek gets some northern nostalgia as he remembers three of his best walks in north Wales. Cadair Idris is a mountain steeped in legend and mythology - it's also one of Wales's most spectacular summits. Derek climbs to three peaks in this range and even braves an icy cold dip in its glacial lake, where the temperature, quite literally, takes his breath away. The second walk Derek recalls is from the Italianate village of Portmeirion, where he also discovers Y Gwyllt - ‘the wild’ headland beyond. Finally, Derek walks the Dee Valley Way, a stunning 13-mile route which takes him from the pretty town of Corwen to its larger and more bustling neighbour, Llangollen. On the walk, he learns of a warrior prince and leads a horse-drawn barge along the Llangollen canal.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites

Bryn Williams celebrates the best of the season's produce with a delicious butternut squash and chestnut tart, served with a winter salad and crispy deep-fried sage leaves. Selin Kaizim brings a taste of Cyprus to the studio with her beef and bulgur wheat koftes, while David Carter makes aubergines the stars of the show. Julie Lin makes a dish packed with crispy fried fish, cucumber, melted cheese, a punchy sambal and a side of crinkle-cut fries. Poppy O’Toole adds spices and harissa to a classic cottage pie base before topping with a fresh chilli and herb mash. And Bryan Cranston and Marianne Jean-Baptiste battle it out for their food heaven. Meanwhile, Rick Stein sets out to prove that old-fashioned veg is best, and the Hairy Bikers learn the history behind one of the world’s most famous condiments in Menorca.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Eva and her Breton guide Tanguy Thomassin explore the vast oyster beds of Cancale, oyster capital of Brittany. Being pummelled by one of the highest tides in Europe makes for fatter, sweeter and healthier oysters. And having once supplied King Louis XVI’s oyster habit, Brittany still supplies half of France. Bretons also boast of plentiful sardines, kelp forests, spiny crabs and the rare cobalt blue lobster. Fished sustainably and cooked on a grill, it's little wonder that this beauty is called the king of lobsters.

programme.title: Natural World

Reinstating the old Caledonian pine forests is the first of his plans. He then wants to release long-lost animals, starting with moose and wild boar, and eventually predators such as brown bears, lynx and wolves. Some of the local people are far from convinced by Paul's vision. Will he even be allowed to let loose moose in the glen?

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Sitting between Germany and France, Alsace is frontier land with a cuisine to match. In Strasbourg, Eva stops off at Brasserie Le Tigre for a beer (brassier means ‘to brew’) and a deliciously creamy tarte flambee. Then there's a trip to guide Coralie Andt’s restaurant, known as a winstub, where French wines can be enjoyed with plenty of cheese and sausage – as well as more sausage with sauerkraut cooked in white Riesling wine. With French tarts in a brasserie that serves German-style beer, and German sausage in a winstub serving French white wine, Alsace is defined by its competing national influences.

programme.title: The Balkans: Europe’s Forgotten Frontier

With Russia’s increasing aggression, Nato’s role in eastern Europe has been beefed up, and Romania has become strategically significant. Katya’s next stop is Europe’s youngest country, Kosovo. She travels down Tony Blair Street – named after the UK prime minister who led the Nato mission there. Twenty-five years after the war ended, Katya meets the ethnic Serbs who still live in Kosovo – and insist the country is still Serbian. Lastly, in Serbia, she visits a coal power plant and discovers there’s a battle for power taking place, with the west, Russia and China all wanting Serbia to be in their sphere of influence. For decades, the west has ignored this corner of Europe, but now, with so many other parts of the world gaining power and influence, the fear is Europe might be losing its foothold in this increasingly important region.
